userStories.title: Thread kind data and REPO-only guard
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist thread kind and nullable repo fields, migrate existing threads safely, and narrow every API REPO-only consumer through one guard.

**Motivation** — Today a thread cannot exist without `repoId`, `baseRef`, `feature` and `specPath` (`apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:1058-1095`), the create route requires a repo and a feature (`apps/api/src/fleet/threads/thread-input.ts`), and the runner always acquires git credentials and prepares a worktree before it opens a session (`apps/runner/src/thread/thread-job-run.ts:217-330`).

**Approach** — API data and REPO-only guard (US-002)

- `ChatThread` (`apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:1058-1095`) — Target: gains `kind String @default("REPO") // REPO | PROJECT`; `repoId`, `baseRef`, `feature`, `specPath` become `String?`; the `repo` relation becomes optional. New migration `apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261017090000_chat_thread_kind/migration.sql` (sorts after the latest, `20261016090000_fleet_job_workflow`): adds the column with default `'REPO'` and drops NOT NULL on the four columns. The partial unique index `ChatThread_active_repo_feature_key` is unchanged (it admits any number of null `repoId` rows).
- `ChatThreadRecord` (`apps/api/src/fleet/threads/domain/chat-thread.domain.ts:46-58`) — Target: gains `kind: ChatThreadKind`; `repoId`, `baseRef`, `feature`, `specPath` become `string | null`. `ThreadDto` (`dto/thread.dto.ts`) mirrors it (`kind` with `enum: ['REPO', 'PROJECT']`; the four fields `nullable: true`). `mapThread` (`prisma-chat-thread.repository.ts:397-409`) maps `kind`; a stored value other than `PROJECT` maps to `REPO`.
- `repoThreadFields(thread: { kind: string; repoId: string | null; baseRef: string | null; feature: string | null; specPath: string | null }): { repoId: string; baseRef: string; feature: string; specPath: string }` — new, in `chat-thread.domain.ts`. Throws `ConflictAppException({}, 'threads.notRepoThread')` (409) only when `kind === 'PROJECT'` or any of the four fields is null; otherwise returns the four fields. A missing or unknown `kind` is treated as `REPO`, matching `mapThread` (existing unit fixtures build thread rows without `kind`). Every REPO-only consumer reads the fields through it:
  - `ThreadsService.plan` and `ThreadsService.run` (`threads.service.ts:87-115`): call it right after the not-found check, before the creator check.
  - `PrismaChatThreadRepository.publish` and `discard` (`prisma-chat-thread.repository.ts:171-255`): call it on the first read row right after its not-found check (`:181` and the matching line in `discard`), before the creator check.
  - `PrismaChatThreadRepository.createThreadJob` (`:354-381`) for a REPO thread (the PROJECT branch is US-004; until then a PROJECT send answers 409 `threads.notRepoThread`).
  - `findThreadAssign` (`prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts:201-215`) uses `thread.feature ?? `thread-${turn.threadId}`` (1a-R1).
  - The thread-ingest cost event (`threads/ingest/prisma-thread-ingest.repository.ts:256-270`, `costEventData`): its `thread` argument gains `id` (the two call sites at `:201` and `:249` add `id` to the thread select), and `featureName` becomes `thread.feature ?? `thread-${thread.id}``.
  - `jobGateKeys` (`apps/api/src/fleet/budgets/budget-rules.ts:40-47`) — Baseline: `repoId: string`, always emits a `repo:<id>` key. Target: `repoId: string | null`; null emits no `repo:` key (project, runner and global keys unchanged). The `thread` parameter of `sendRefusalFor` (`prisma-chat-thread.repository.ts:316`) widens `repoId` to `string | null` the same way. In US-002 both still receive `thread.repoId` as stored (null for a PROJECT row); US-004 swaps in the anchor.
- i18n (`apps/api/src/i18n/{en,zh}/threads.json`): new key `notRepoThread`.

1a-R3: PROJECT threads have no Publish, Discard, Plan or Run. The routes answer 409 `threads.notRepoThread`; the web hides the action bar.

1a-R4: the kind rule (REPO has `repoId`, `baseRef`, `feature`, `specPath`; PROJECT has none) is enforced by the create path, the only writer of those columns. No database check constraint: integration schemas are built with `prisma db push` (`apps/api/test/helpers/partial-indexes.ts`), which cannot create one.

Compatibility note: the stated helper signature describes persisted rows; its call surface must also permit the AC's missing-kind fixture and treat it as REPO. Do not require a kind at runtime for old fixtures. Update the typed ChatThreadRecord literal in threads.service.spec.ts with kind: 'REPO'; other expectations unchanged. Regenerate Prisma client and openapi.json for kind and nullable response fields. Test migration SQL with scratchSchemaBefore/applyMigration, not only db push. US-002 owns every API nullable-column compile site listed above so this story is independently usable before PROJECT create/send exists.

**Scope** — In: ChatThread migration/schema/domain/response, REPO-only guard and guard precedence, nullable budgets/ASSIGN/cost fallbacks, localized conflict and existing fixture updates. Out: PROJECT create validation/anchor lookup (US-003), PROJECT session branch and anchor budgeting (US-004), emitted ASSIGN kind/placement (US-005), runner/web changes (US-006/007); no FleetJob schema changes, SQL check constraint or thread conversion.

**Interface** — The persisted-row signature quoted above is widened at the helper's callable boundary to make the missing-kind fixture in AC3 type-safe:
```ts
repoThreadFields(thread: { kind?: string; repoId: string | null; baseRef: string | null; feature: string | null; specPath: string | null }): { repoId: string; baseRef: string; feature: string; specPath: string }
```
Only the helper input kind is optional; persisted ChatThreadRecord.kind remains required. Missing or unknown kind with four non-null fields returns those fields unchanged, and PROJECT or any null field still throws the specified conflict.

userStories.title: Create PROJECT threads
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Allow authorized project developers to create native PROJECT threads with null repo fields when a deterministic anchor repo exists.

**Motivation** — A user would have to pick a repo and an unused feature name just to chat, and every session would clone and check out a repo it never reads.

**Approach** — API create (US-003)

- `validateCreateThread` (`apps/api/src/fleet/threads/thread-input.ts`) — Baseline: `validateCreateThread(value: CreateThreadInput, defaultBranch: string): Omit<CreateThreadInput, 'baseRef' | 'maxCostUsd'> & { baseRef: string; maxCostUsd: string }`. Target:

```ts
export interface CreateThreadInput { kind?: ChatThreadKind; repoId?: string; feature?: string; baseRef?: string; title: string; maxCostUsd?: number; backend: ThreadBackend }
export type NormalizedCreateThread =
  | { kind: 'REPO'; repoId: string; feature: string; baseRef: string; title: string; maxCostUsd: string; backend: ThreadBackend }
  | { kind: 'PROJECT'; title: string; maxCostUsd: string; backend: ThreadBackend & { kind: 'native' } };
export function validateCreateThread(value: CreateThreadInput, defaultBranch: string): NormalizedCreateThread;
```

  Checks, in order, first failure wins: `kind` (absent means `REPO`; any other value than `REPO` / `PROJECT` fails with reason `kind`); for `REPO`, a missing or non-string `repoId` fails with reason `repoId` (new rule), then today's `feature`, `baseRef` checks; for `PROJECT`, any of `repoId`, `feature`, `baseRef` present fails with reason `projectFields`; then today's `title`, `maxCostUsd`, `backend` checks; for `PROJECT`, a backend of kind `acp` fails with reason `backend`. All failures are `ValidationAppException({ reason }, 'threads.input')` (400).
- `CreateThreadDto` (`dto/thread.dto.ts`) — Target: gains `kind?` (`enum: ['REPO', 'PROJECT']`); `repoId` and `feature` become `required: false`.
- `ChatThreadRepository.create` input (`chat-thread.domain.ts:62`) and `PrismaChatThreadRepository.create` (`prisma-chat-thread.repository.ts:48-56`) — Target: input is `{ kind: ChatThreadKind; projectId; repoId: string | null; baseRef: string | null; feature: string | null; title; createdById; backend; skills; maxCostUsd }`; `specPath` is `.nax/features/<feature>/spec.md` for REPO and `null` for PROJECT.
- `ThreadsService.create` (`threads.service.ts:27-40`) — Target: calls `validateCreateThread` once for PROJECT (no repo lookup). For PROJECT it resolves the anchor through `IFleetRepoRepository.findAnchor(projectId)`; null answers `ConflictAppException({}, 'threads.noFleetRepo')` (409); otherwise it creates the thread with `kind: 'PROJECT'` and null repo fields. REPO keeps today's two-pass flow.
- `IFleetRepoRepository.findAnchor(projectId: string): Promise<FleetRepoRecord | null>` — new (`apps/api/src/fleet/repos/domain/fleet-repo.domain.ts`, implemented in `prisma-fleet-repo.repository.ts`): the project's repo with the smallest `createdAt`, ties broken by the smallest `id`; null when the project has none.
- i18n: new key `noFleetRepo` in `threads.json` (en + zh).

S5b-R3: a `PROJECT` thread has no repo, worktree or feature. `REPO` threads keep all S5a behaviour.

1a-R2: PROJECT threads with an ACP backend are refused at creation (ACP sessions get no tools, nax#2444).

The kill switch is unchanged: `FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED` gates PROJECT threads exactly as it gates REPO threads.

Keep current controller human-principal, ProjectMembershipGuard and CREATE FleetJob CASL authorization; PROJECT is not a new permission bypass. Snapshot skills as today. The anchor existence check must not populate ChatThread.repoId or any repo-specific thread field. Update prisma-chat-thread.repository.spec.ts's existing create call with kind: 'REPO', preserving its expectations. Extend test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts with POST /api/projects/:slug/threads kind PROJECT 201 and kind PROJECT plus feature 400. Regenerate openapi.json for kind and optional create fields and refresh the CLI through generation. Write unit input tests alongside existing service tests and real Postgres anchor/create integration tests.

**Scope** — In: discriminated normalization, create DTO/service/repository fields, deterministic public anchor lookup, localized no-repo conflict and endpoint lifecycle behavior. Out: transactional send anchor helper, session instructions/jobs/budget substitution (US-004), ASSIGN/placement (US-005), runner (US-006), web (US-007); ACP PROJECT sessions and WORKSPACE are not enabled.

**Interface** —
```ts
IFleetRepoRepository.findAnchor(projectId: string): Promise<FleetRepoRecord | null>
```
The CreateThreadInput, NormalizedCreateThread and validateCreateThread declarations above are the target create contract.

userStories.title: PROJECT session job on the anchor repo
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Dispatch PROJECT conversation sessions using the deterministic bookkeeping anchor with project-only instructions and consistent budget/activity/cost accounting.

**Motivation** — The koda assistant (S5b) must answer questions such as "which tickets are blocked?" that have nothing to do with a repo checkout.

**Approach** — API session job (US-004)

- `anchorRepoFor(projectId)` — a private helper of `PrismaChatThreadRepository` with the same rule as `findAnchor`.
- `createThreadJob` (`prisma-chat-thread.repository.ts:354-381`) — Target: for a PROJECT thread it resolves the anchor inside the send transaction; none answers 409 `threads.noFleetRepo`; the job gets `repoId` = anchor id and `ref` = anchor `defaultBranch`; the instructions come from `buildProjectThreadInstructions` with the project's slug.
- `sendRefusalFor` (`:316-334`) and `sendRefusalOf` (`:84-97`) — Target: `sendRefusalFor`'s `thread` parameter gains `kind` (passed by `sendRefusalOf` and by `sendMessage`); for a PROJECT thread the budget gate keys use the anchor's id, or `null` when the project has no fleet repo. The no-repo case is not a send refusal: GET detail answers 200 with the usual `sendRefusal`, and the send itself then answers 409 `threads.noFleetRepo` from `createThreadJob`.
- Job-dispatch activity payload (`:304`) — Target: for a PROJECT thread `payload.repoId` is the anchor's id and `payload.ref` its default branch.
- `buildProjectThreadInstructions(input: { project: string; skills: ThreadSkillSource[] }): string` — new, in `apps/api/src/fleet/threads/thread-instructions.ts`. Worked shape:

```ts
export function buildProjectThreadInstructions(input: { project: string; skills: ThreadSkillSource[] }): string {
  const lines = [
    `You are a brainstorming partner for the koda project "${input.project}". This thread is not tied to a repository.`,
    'Ask one question at a time. You have no repository, no shell and no web access; do not claim facts about code you cannot see.',
  ];
  // then the same "Skills available" block as buildThreadInstructions
}
```

  The text never mentions `write_doc`, `list_files`, `search_repo` or Publish.

S5b-R13 (anchor repo): `FleetJob.repoId`, `ref` and `feature` stay required. A PROJECT thread's THREAD job uses the project's **anchor repo** — its oldest `FleetRepo` by `createdAt`, then smallest `id` — as `repoId`, the anchor's `defaultBranch` as `ref`, and `thread-<threadId>` as `feature` (as every THREAD job already does). The anchor is bookkeeping only (placement, budget keys, dashboards, activity); the runner never clones, fetches or touches it and requests no git token for the job. A project with no fleet repo cannot create or run a PROJECT thread (409 `threads.noFleetRepo`).

Retain the existing transaction, job/thread locks, duplicate clientMessageId behavior, remaining-cost Prisma.Decimal calculation, thread pinning/resume and post-commit placement/notifier boundaries. Derive activity repoId/ref from the anchor job, not the null thread fields. Reuse the exact skill-list formatting of buildThreadInstructions. The nullable cost event fallback was implemented in US-002: verify the turn_end path through real ingest produces featureName thread-<threadId>, including id in both cost lookup selections. No existing REPO expectations change.

SEAM-2 (US-003 -> US-004): `IFleetRepoRepository.findAnchor`'s rule is what thread job creation applies; a US-004 AC triggers `POST /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id/messages` and asserts the job's `repoId` is the oldest repo's id.
SEAM-3 (US-004): `buildProjectThreadInstructions` is called by thread job creation; US-004 ACs trigger `POST /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id/messages` and assert the stored `FleetThreadTurn.instructions`.

**Scope** — In: transactional PROJECT SESSION job branch, private anchor lookup, project instructions, detail/send refusal anchor budgeting, dispatch activity and PROJECT cost-ingest verification. Out: create validation/public anchor lookup (US-003), ASSIGN kind and placement capability (US-005), no-checkout runner session (US-006), UI (US-007); no FleetJob schema changes or koda data tools. Anchor repo budget gates are explicitly in scope: a pause on that repo must stop PROJECT sends. Removing that accepted coupling is out of scope. US-004 only: budget pauses scoped to the anchor repo also stop PROJECT threads; this coupling is accepted (S5b-R13). Existing repo deletion/resume side effects are accepted, not redesigned.

**Interface** —
```ts
export function buildProjectThreadInstructions(input: { project: string; skills: ThreadSkillSource[] }): string
```
Private `anchorRepoFor(projectId)` follows `findAnchor`: createdAt ascending, then id ascending, null when absent.

userStories.title: PROJECT ASSIGN and placement
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry normalized thread kind into ASSIGN and both placement paths so only capable runners host PROJECT sessions.

**Motivation** — The koda assistant (S5b) must answer questions such as "which tickets are blocked?" that have nothing to do with a repo checkout.

**Approach** — API ASSIGN and placement (US-005)

- `findThreadAssign` (`prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts:201-215`) — Target: also selects the thread's `kind` and returns `kind` (`PROJECT` when the row says `PROJECT`, otherwise `REPO`); `feature` per 1a-R1.
- `toPlacementJob` (`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/placement-rules.ts:163-170`) and `PlacementJob.thread` (`:24-33`) — Target: the thread argument gains `kind?: ChatThreadKind`. Both builders pass the assign's `kind`: `PlacementService.placeJob` (`placement.service.ts:85-86`, reached right after a send commits) and `PlacementService.fillRunnerThreads` (`:165`, reached from a runner sync).
- `firstMisfit` THREAD branch (`placement-rules.ts:108-125`) — Target: right after the `protocol` check, a job whose `thread.kind` is `PROJECT` on a runner whose `capabilities.projectThreads !== true` returns the new `MisfitReason` `'project_threads'`. Not in `PERMANENT_MISFITS`. The value is added to `MisfitReason`, the `PlacementMisfitDto.reason` enum (`jobs/dto/fleet-job.dto.ts:127`) and the dashboard list (`dashboard/dashboard.types.ts:109-111`).

S5b-R9: no protocol version bump. The ASSIGN `thread` block gains an optional `kind`; a runner advertises `projectThreads: true`; PROJECT THREAD jobs are placed only on runners that advertise it.

1a-R1: the API always sends `thread.kind` (`REPO` or `PROJECT`) on a THREAD ASSIGN. A runner treats a missing `kind` as `REPO`. `ThreadAssign.feature` stays a required string: for a PROJECT thread the API sends `thread-<threadId>` (the job's own feature), and the runner never uses it for a PROJECT run. This keeps the runner's existing `feature: string` consumers (`thread-worktree.ts`, `thread-publish.ts`, `thread-action-run.ts`) unchanged.

Use the US-002 fallback `thread.feature ?? `thread-${turn.threadId}``. ASSIGN still carries the required repo block for the anchor; it does not change PROJECT thread.repoId. Preserve normal backend matching, thread capacity, protocol precedence, budget gating, casAssign, pinning, transitions and post-commit notification. An unavailable PROJECT capability is recoverable, not permanent, so unsupported runners leave the job QUEUED. Regenerate openapi.json for PlacementMisfitDto.reason and the dashboard misfit enum; do not invent a protocol bump or alter existing REPO placements.

SEAM-1 (US-001 -> US-005): `parseCapabilitiesCore` stores `projectThreads`; US-005 ACs post a capability report through `POST /api/fleet/runner/sync` and assert placement of a PROJECT THREAD job.

userStories.title: Runner no-checkout path for PROJECT threads
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Run PROJECT sessions in a safe scratch directory with only skill tools and no anchor git credential or checkout operations.

**Motivation** — A user would have to pick a repo and an unused feature name just to chat, and every session would clone and check out a repo it never reads.

**Approach** — Runner (US-006)

- `parseAssign` thread block (`apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts:148-188`) — Target: reads optional `kind`; a present value other than `REPO` or `PROJECT` returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid thread kind' }`. A `PROJECT` block with an action other than `SESSION` returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid thread action' }`. `feature` is checked as today for every kind. The parsed `ThreadAssign` carries `kind` as received (absent stays absent).
- Capability probe (`apps/runner/src/capabilities/nax-probe.ts:156-170`) — Target: the report gains `projectThreads: true`.
- `threadScratchDir(homeDir: string, threadId: string): string` — new in `apps/runner/src/thread/thread-paths.ts`: `join(threadDirFor(homeDir, threadId), 'scratch')`. It lives under the thread directory, so `pruneThreads` removes it with the thread.
- `buildProjectThreadTools(ctx: ThreadToolContext): EmbedderTool[]` — new in `apps/runner/src/thread/tools/index.ts`: `[loadSkillTool(ctx), readSkillFileTool(ctx)]`. The PROJECT run builds the full `ThreadToolContext` as the REPO path does, with `worktree` = the scratch dir and no `feature` / `onDocWritten`; the two factories keep their signatures.
- `ThreadJobRun.run` SESSION path (`apps/runner/src/thread/thread-job-run.ts:217-330`) — Target: when `thread.kind === 'PROJECT'` it skips step 1 (`credentials.acquire`) and steps 2-4 (`prepare`), creates `threadScratchDir(homeDir, threadId)` (recursive; no error when it exists), runs step 5 (skills) unchanged, opens the session with `worktree` = that scratch dir and `tools` = `buildProjectThreadTools({ worktree: scratch, skillsRoot, skills, git, searchTimeoutMs, nowMs })`, opens the stream with `stale` false, and creates no `ThreadLivePublish`. `command('THREAD_PUBLISH', …)` on such a run returns `{ result: 'rejected', detail: 'not_repo_thread' }`. REPO runs are unchanged.

1a-R1: the API always sends `thread.kind` (`REPO` or `PROJECT`) on a THREAD ASSIGN. A runner treats a missing `kind` as `REPO`. `ThreadAssign.feature` stays a required string: for a PROJECT thread the API sends `thread-<threadId>` (the job's own feature), and the runner never uses it for a PROJECT run. This keeps the runner's existing `feature: string` consumers (`thread-worktree.ts`, `thread-publish.ts`, `thread-action-run.ts`) unchanged.

The anchor is bookkeeping only (placement, budget keys, dashboards, activity); the runner never clones, fetches or touches it and requests no git token for the job. Retain common skill setup, session initialization, cancellation/halt checks, bounded session close, transcript/resume behavior, heartbeat/idle/cost limits, log shipping/drain and legal transitions. Skill-cache fetches are unchanged; they are not a checkout of the anchor. Use threadDirFor's safe-segment validation rather than constructing paths from untrusted thread ids. Do not add network calls outside established runner transport seams. PROJECT never creates ThreadLivePublish, and does not call REPO prepare/publish/action helpers. Update the nax-probe.spec.ts whole capability expectation with projectThreads: true; other expectations unchanged. Use temp filesystem, injected seams and the real journal in focused runner tests; preserve the existing REPO and missing-kind paths.

SEAM-5 (US-001 -> US-006): `ThreadAssign.kind` from the package is what the runner parser reads; US-006 ACs drive `parseAssign` with a PROJECT thread block, and start a `ThreadJobRun` from it.

**Scope** — In: runner payload validation, advertised capability, scratch path helper, skill-only tools and PROJECT SESSION setup/command rejection. Out: API schema/create/send/placement (US-002 through US-005), web (US-007), koda tool proxies and ACP PROJECT support; no ThreadAssign.feature optionality, protocol version bump, PROJECT repository tools, Publish/Discard/Plan/Run or anchor checkout.

**Interface** —
```ts
threadScratchDir(homeDir: string, threadId: string): string
buildProjectThreadTools(ctx: ThreadToolContext): EmbedderTool[]
```
Invalid kind: `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid thread kind' }`. Invalid PROJECT action: `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid thread action' }`. PROJECT live publish: `{ result: 'rejected', detail: 'not_repo_thread' }`.

[unit] In thread-job-run-project.spec.ts, starting a ThreadJobRun for a PROJECT SESSION ASSIGN calls the session opener with worktree equal to threadScratchDir(homeDir, threadId).
[unit] Starting a ThreadJobRun for a PROJECT SESSION ASSIGN calls the session opener with tools whose names are exactly ['load_skill', 'read_skill_file'].

userStories.title: Web scope picker and PROJECT thread rendering
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let users choose Repo or Project scope and render PROJECT identity without repo fields or the REPO action bar.

**Motivation** — A user would have to pick a repo and an unused feature name just to chat, and every session would clone and check out a repo it never reads.

**Approach** — Web (US-007)

- `ThreadDto` (`apps/web/lib/thread-types.ts:77-104`) — Target: gains `kind: 'REPO' | 'PROJECT'`; `repoId`, `baseRef`, `feature`, `specPath` become `string | null`. `FleetRunnerSummary` (`apps/web/lib/fleet-types.ts:102-112`) gains `projectThreads: boolean`.
- `apps/web/lib/thread-create.ts` — Target: `ThreadCreateValues` gains `kind: 'REPO' | 'PROJECT'`. `buildThreadCreateSchema` adds `kind: z.enum(['REPO', 'PROJECT']).default('REPO')` and moves the `repoId`, `baseRef` and `feature` rules into a `superRefine` that runs them only when `kind` is `REPO` (same message keys), adding each issue with `path: ['repoId']`, `['baseRef']` or `['feature']` so the form shows it on that field. `toCreateThreadBody` returns `{ kind: 'PROJECT', title, maxCostUsd, backend }` for PROJECT and today's body plus `kind: 'REPO'` for REPO. `eligibleModels(runners, kind)` gains a `kind` argument; for `PROJECT` it keeps only runners whose `projectThreads` is true.

Keep existing online/enabled filtering, model deduplication/sorting, shared title/cost/model/effort validation, default branch placeholder, skill display, role-gated create presentation and the models watcher. **Scope** — In: mirrored DTO types, scope-aware schema/body/model selection, native scope picker, PROJECT feature labels, hidden action bar and en/zh strings with unit/component coverage. Out: backend creation/anchor behavior (US-003/004), placement (US-005), runner execution (US-006); no anchor display, general navigation/layout/token redesign, koda data tools or Playwright PROJECT journey.

analysis:
This is an enhancement to the existing S5a thread implementation, not a greenfield assistant. Goal: introduce PROJECT threads belonging only to a project, carry their kind from creation through ASSIGN to the runner and web, and host their conversations with skill tools but without an anchor checkout or git credential request. Done means all seven stories and their behavioral criteria are satisfied while existing REPO thread behavior remains unchanged. This is only S5b-1a; the umbrella design's later data tools and personal workspace threads must not leak into implementation.

Discovery and architecture: codebase-memory MCP was unavailable in this session, so discovery used direct repository reads, Glob and Grep. References below are verified against current files rather than trusting the spec's baseline line numbers. The supplied framework detection is inaccurate: apps/api/src/fleet/threads/threads.controller.ts:1-23 uses NestJS controllers, Swagger, ProjectMembershipGuard and Nathapp primitives; .nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:17-29 specifies NestJS 12 + Fastify, Prisma 7 and Vitest. .nax/mono/apps/web/context.md:19-28 and apps/web/pages/[project]/threads/new.vue:1-12 establish Nuxt 3/Vue, vee-validate/Zod and Jest, not Next.js. The runner is Bun-only ESM; .nax/mono/apps/runner/context.md:19-22 specifies bun:sqlite and bun test. Read each app context before implementation and the nathapp-nestjs-patterns skill before writing NestJS code. Do not edit generated AGENTS.md or generated CLI files. All paths in this PRD are repository-rooted. Binding workdirs/dependencies take precedence over the general single-package rule: US-001 remains workdir apps/api even though it also edits packages/fleet-protocol.

Shared rulings for every story: S5b-R3 means a PROJECT ChatThread has null repoId/baseRef/feature/specPath and no worktree, while REPO retains S5a behavior. S5b-R13 leaves FleetJob.repoId/ref/feature required: the anchor is the project's oldest FleetRepo ordered by createdAt ascending, id ascending; its id/defaultBranch become the job repoId/ref, and the job feature is thread-<threadId>. The anchor exists for bookkeeping, placement, budget scopes, dashboards and activity only and must never be exposed as the thread's repo or touched by the PROJECT runner. Creation and new session sends without any fleet repo return 409 threads.noFleetRepo. S5b-R9 keeps FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION at 4: optional ThreadAssign.kind plus projectThreads?: true provide compatibility. The API always emits kind; absent or unknown stored kind maps to REPO; a runner treats absent kind as REPO but rejects an explicitly unknown kind. ThreadAssign.feature stays required string and PROJECT gets thread-<threadId>; do not loosen downstream REPO worktree/publish/action consumers. Use ChatThreadKind rather than ThreadKind because isThreadKind already classifies THREAD job commands. PROJECT only accepts native backends, has only SESSION actions, and never offers Publish/Discard/Plan/Run. FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED and all existing project/user/creator authorization remain intact. The kind/field invariant is enforced by the only column writer, creation, with no SQL check constraint. Repo is the default form scope.

US-001 impact and dependencies: packages/fleet-protocol/src/threads.ts:1-40 currently defines isThreadKind, ThreadBackend and ThreadAssign with required feature but no chat kind. packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts:9-17 exports threads and fixes protocol at 4; RunnerCapabilities at :64-82 contains optional threadBackends/threadWrite. Modify existing common/capabilities-thread.spec.ts, common/thread-jobs.spec.ts and runners/dto/runner-summary.dto.spec.ts. PlacementJob.thread at placement-rules.ts:24-33 and toPlacementJob at :163-170 accept optional kind. firstMisfit at :102-130 handles THREAD before ordinary repo tools/mutex/capacity checks; insert project_threads immediately after protocol and before backend/action checks, leave it out of PERMANENT_MISFITS (:20-22), and leave thread capacity behavior intact. Strict capability parsing must neither manufacture false/absent capabilities nor omit the new true flag while cleaning reports. Anchor selection must be deterministic on tied timestamps and consistent between create and transactional send; repo deletion after creation must not cascade-delete PROJECT threads. Accepted existing deletion semantics are active-anchor job deletion refusal and idle-anchor deletion removing old jobs/turns, producing resume false next session. Keep budget/refusal reads safe with no anchor and do not turn detail reads into errors. Lifecycle branching must never accidentally acquire credentials, clone/fetch the anchor, expose repository tools, create a live publisher or break existing cancellation/log/session shutdown behavior. Preserve human/project/creator authorization and exact guard precedence. SEAM-1 verifies sync capability persistence to placement; SEAM-2 asserts anchor selection via HTTP send and stored job; SEAM-3 asserts project instructions via stored turn after HTTP send; SEAM-4 verifies both placeJob and fillRunnerThreads; SEAM-5 drives parseAssign into the PROJECT ThreadJobRun. Binding dependency graph is US-001 -> US-002 -> US-003 -> US-004 -> US-005, plus US-006 after US-001 and US-007 after US-003; no story merges, splits or extra stories. Roll out additive protocol support first, then the nullable schema and API creation/session/placement, with runner capability advertising and web scope UI gated by those contracts.
